final_message:
`mrr` in `billing/reports.py` was filtering subscriptions on `subscription["customer_id"]` instead of `subscription["status"]`. No customer ID is ever `"active"` or `"past_due"`, so every subscription was skipped and the report came back empty. I changed it to check `status`.

The full suite passes (25 tests), including your reproduction. I saved that test as `tests/test_reports_bug.py`.

I also wrote `answer.json` in the repo root: `{"file": "reports.py", "function": "mrr"}`.

I didn't run mypy.

steps.command:
echo '{"file": "reports.py", "function": "mrr"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_reports_bug.py <<'EOF'
from billing import reports


def test_mrr_and_aging(world):
    from billing import catalog

    yearly = catalog.create_price(world.ctx, world.plan["id"], "usd", "flat", unit_amount=12000, interval="year")
    a = world.customer()
    b = world.customer(email="b@example.com", card=False)
    world.engine.subscribe(a["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 3)])
    world.engine.subscribe(b["id"], [(yearly["id"], 1)])
    assert reports.mrr(world.ctx) == {"usd": 3000 + 1000}
    world.clock.advance_days(40)
    aging = reports.aging(world.ctx, world.clock.now())
    assert aging["usd"]["31-60"] == 12000
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15
